patch_resolves_note: The best-effort `switch-fixed --patch patch.diff` rebuild in the vulnerable image still reproduced the crash, so fixed-side evidence uses the authoritative `n132/arvo:42473836-fix` image. There the same `BNDLDXrm` witness path reaches `printMemReference()` with `MI->op1_size` already set to 16, skips `MI->op1_size = MI->x86opsize`, and the later sink reads an initialized byte.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First non-harness project statement that consumes the three attacker-controlled instruction bytes and materializes the x86 decode state later printed by the vulnerable x86 formatter.

Root cause. In 32-bit mode the selected register-size table stops at `X86_REG_R15W`. In the same vulnerable commit, `include/capstone/x86.h` and `X86MappingReg.inc` already define public/register-map entries for `X86_REG_BND0..X86_REG_BND3`, so the earlier `printOperand()` lookup for `X86_REG_BND3` has no defined in-bounds 16-byte element to use on this witness path. The fix appends four trailing `16` entries here; the same omission also exists in `regsize_map_64`.

Sink. After `printInstruction()` returns, the left operand of this `&&` reads `MI->op1_size`. The staged MemorySanitizer run reports the corresponding built-tree line 745 in this same condition as the `use-of-uninitialized-value` site.
Immediately after `printMemReference()` executes `MI->op1_size = MI->x86opsize`, the destination byte `MI->op1_size` is still uninitialized on the vulnerable witness path.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `op1_size_copy.op1_size_initialized_prefix_len = 0` and `op1_size_copy.op1_size_store_bytes = 1` immediately after the fallback copy.
